newsitem.title: UK: C&W execs granted 469,000 options at 553.3p.
newsitem.headline: C&W execs granted 469,000 options at 553.3p.

text.p: Three top directors of Cable and Wireless Plc, Britain's second biggest telecom group, and its main subsidiary were on Tuesday given an option to bet on C&W's shares rising above 553.3p between the years 2000 and 2004.

Chief executive Richard Brown, who was paid 1.24 million pounds last year including bonuses, benefits and a relocation allowance, was granted options on 300,000 shares at 553.3p. He now has 922,891 share options.
Stephen Pettit, the executive director for the global business, who earned 447,089 stg last year, was granted 89,000, taking his total options to 315,397.
The company also said Linus Cheung, the chief executive of C&W's subsidiary Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, had been granted 80,000 new options and now held 460,653.
Linus Cheung earned 926,376 stg in the past year, including bonuses, benefits and allowances, such as property on Hong Kong island, worth 419,601 stg.
Directors at C&W are usually granted share options annually by the remuneration committee, which is made up of five, non-executive directors.
But the company has placed a ceiling of four times a director's salary plus performance-related bonus on executive share options, C&W said.

Brown, who was granted just over 600,000 options on joining C&W last July, earned the respect of analysts most recently by securing access to the Chinese mainland in a deal which could give a mainland company the right to take up to 30 percent of Hong Kong Telecom.
C&W's shares surged 15 percent to around 580p 11 days ago on the back of hopes of lucrative telecoms projects in booming China. They were trading at 556.5p, a loss of 5.0p, in the early afternoon.
